postDeltaDatePacketReport.auditSummary: Independent native date audit on PR #5477 @ 88ed7339 with full unit, item, and person coverage. Owner follow-up removed 340 unsupported Ming-table westernBounds; Chinese sourceDates checked in evidence. Chapter remains research-blocked for Western conversion, not unaudited.
postDeltaDatePacketReport.note: 547 supported checks preserved as-is; 340 research-blocked attestation holds were source-event repaired (no Western conversion, no blanket clearance).

diagnosis: Of 340 held unresolved attestations after Ming-table retraction, deterministic scan found 337 invented sourceDate texts absent from owned citation units and 3 literal matches. Repaired at source-event level: replace exact Chinese on owned evidence, expand evidence for adjacent framing dates, refine the 3 literals, or undate witnessed undated events.

perItemPlans.event: In the Jiaping era of Cao Fang, the deposed Prince of Qi of Wei, a horse rumor arose in Dongjun.
Cao Biao, Prince of Chu formerly enfeoffed at Baima, was plotted to be enthroned by Linghu Yu and Wang Ling and was ordered to die.
Yan Province inspector Linghu Yu plotted with Wang Ling to enthrone Cao Biao and was executed.
Wang Ling plotted to enthrone Cao Biao and was executed.
Liu Shan, Later Lord of Shu, succeeded Liu Bei, changed the era before his burial, and surrendered to Wei.
Qiao Zhou read the names Bei and Shan as an omen of Shu's fall.
Liu Bei, the late founder of Shu, died; his name Bei was glossed as "complete".
Emperor Ming of Wei was enshrined as Liezu while living in Jingchu 1 and died two years later.
Jiang Wei defected to Shu in Wei's Taihe era and refused his mother's call to return.
In Sun Xiu's reign in Wu a man of Wucheng acquired a far-carrying voice.
Emperor Wu of Jin (Sima Yan), whose style was Anshi, talked of trivia rather than long-term policy.
He Ceng foretold to his son Zun that the dynasty's heirs were in peril.
He Zun, son of He Ceng, heard his father's prophecy.
He Sui was killed without guilt in the Yongjia era, fulfilling He Ceng's words.
Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, deposed Emperor Hui at Jinyong and was executed.
Emperor Hui was deposed by Sima Lun, restored, and later forced to flee.
Crown Prince Sima Tan was demoted to Prince of Qinghe in Yongxing 1.
Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, was made imperial heir-brother with immense honors and came to a bad end.
Emperor Huai was made imperial heir-brother and later died a captive.
Jiang Wei's mother was made to write calling him back from Shu.
A Wucheng man recovered from illness able to project his voice for miles.
The neighbor used the voice to dun a debtor.
Emperor Wu's empress lived in Anshi Hall.
Emperor Yuan of Jin was attacked by Wang Dun in his last years.
Grand General Wang Dun occupied Gushu in Yongchang 2, attacked the capital and rebelled again under Emperor Ming.
Emperor Ming of Jin faced Wang Dun's second plot while in mourning.
Qian Feng's rebel army was checked by the royal troops.
Shen Chong's rebel army was checked by the royal troops.
Northern General of the Household Liu Xia led the Huai-Si forces to rescue the court.
Huailing administrator Su Jun led the Huai-Si forces to rescue the court.
In the time of the Duke of Haixi, Yu Xi sang dirges.
Yu Xi loved singing dirges and later fell.
Wang Guobao attacked his clansman Wang Xiaobo.
Wang Xiaobo fought his clansman Wang Guobao.
Huan Xuan usurped the throne and changed the era to Daheng, Jianshi and Yongshi.
Sima Daozi was exiled to Ancheng by Huan Xuan.
Emperor An abdicated and was made Prince of Pinggu.
Sima Dewen, Prince of Langya, was made Duke of Shiyang and sent to Xunyang.
He Zeng disdained the imperial kitchens early in Emperor Wu's reign.
He Shao, son of He Zeng, exceeded his father in luxury.
Wang Kai exceeded He Shao in luxury and was outdone by Shi Chong.
Yang Xiu lavished wealth on music and women.
Shi Chong's extravagance rivaled the ruler; he was executed.
Emperor Ming of Wei saw drought in Taihe 2 and died the year before Zhengshi 1.
Sima Yi captured Meng Da, was made Grand Tutor by Cao Shuang, and overshadowed the Wei court.
Meng Da was captured by Sima Yi.
Zhang He defeated Zhuge Liang and killed Ma Su.
Zhuge Liang was defeated by Zhang He.
Ma Su was killed after his defeat.
In Cao Fang's Zhengshi 1 there was drought.
Cao Shuang moved Sima Yi to Grand Tutor to monopolize power.
In Cao Mao's Ganlu 3 there was drought.
Sima Zhao besieged Zhuge Dan at Shouchun.
Zhuge Dan held Shouchun until it fell.
In Sun Liang's Wufeng 2 Wu suffered drought.
Sun Hao moved the Wu capital to Wuchang in Baoding 1.
Emperor Wu of Jin heeded Xun Xu and selected ministers' daughters for the harem.
Xun Xu's slander kept Jia Chong at court.
Jia Chong was kept from his western command.
Ren Kai was gradually distanced.
Li Xi was left in a sinecure.
Lu Zhi was left in a sinecure.
Li Yin was left in a sinecure.
Zhuge Chong's daughters were selected for the palace.
Minister of Works Sima You, Prince of Qi, reviewed prisoners in Taikang 3.
Daughters of Zhuge Chong and other officers were selected for the palace.
Liu Yi memorialized against partisan ministers in Taikang 5; the emperor did not answer.
Emperor Wu of Jin ignored Liu Yi and trusted Jia Chong, Xun Xu, Yang Jun and Feng Dan.
Xun Xu wielded power abusively at court.
Feng Dan wielded power abusively at court.
Jia Chong held key office in the Taikang era.
Yang Jun held key office in the Taikang era.
Drought struck in Emperor Hui's Yuankang 7.
Yong Province inspector Jie Xi was defeated by the Di and Qiang.
Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, was attacked by three princes in Yongning 1.
Drought struck in Emperor Huai's Yongjia 3.
Sima Yue seized and killed Miu Bo and others and later ignored ceremony with his mobile headquarters.
Secretariat Director Miu Bo was seized and killed by Sima Yue.
Liu Yuanhai ravaged the people.
Shi Le ravaged the people.
Wang Mi ravaged the people.
Li Xiong ravaged the people.
Drought struck in Emperor Yuan's Jianwu 1 and Taixing 4.
Chunyu Bo was unjustly executed, followed by drought.
Gan Bao said drought followed Chunyu Bo's execution for three years.
Wang Dun's usurpation grew evident and he staged the Shitou incident.
Drought struck in Emperor Ming's Taining 3.
Emperor Cheng was a child when Empress Dowager Yu ruled.
Empress Dowager Yu (Mingmu) ruled as regent.
Wang Dao declined the post of Grand Tutor and returned rule to the emperor, and governed leniently.
Drought struck in Emperor Kang's Jianyuan 1.
Emperor Mu was an infant when Empress Dowager Chu ruled.
Empress Dowager Chu ruled as regent for Emperor Mu.
Drought struck in Emperor Ai's Longhe 1.
Huan Wen dominated the court and was honored at Gaoping mausoleum.
Drought struck in the Duke of Haixi's Taihe 1.
Drought struck in Emperor Jianwen's Xian'an 1.
Drought struck in Emperor Xiaowu's Ningkang 1.
Fu Jian was defeated in Taiyuan 8.
Yang Liang attacked Ba and Mian.
Zhao Tong attacked Ba and Mian.
Xie An went to command Guangling and sent his son Yan to Pengcheng.
Xie Yan, son of Xie An, advanced to Pengcheng.
Guo Quan garrisoned Yewang.
Three princes attacked Sima Lun in sixty days of battles.
Emperor Xiaowu (Liezong) was lenient and trusted Sima Daozi.
Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, governed laxly.
Ru Qianqiu, adviser to the Cavalry General, abused the authority of prince and throne.
Drought struck in Emperor An's Long'an 2.
Source-dated attestation retained from Chinese “隆安五年以後”; Western bound retracted.
Huan Xuan forced Yin Zhongkan's death, lived extravagantly, and usurped the throne.
Yin Zhongkan was forced to his death by Huan Xuan.
Sima Yuanxian demanded that all officials show him reverence.
In Emperor Ming of Wei's Taihe era a song foretold the Cao clan's fall; dying, he summoned Sima Yi.
Cao Shuang was executed and the Cao clan deposed.
Sima Yi returned from Liaodong and raced east to the dying emperor, as the rhyme of "Grandpa" foretold.
In the Prince of Qi's Jiaping era a rhyme about a white horse arose.
Cao Biao, Prince of Chu, nicknamed Zhu Hu (Red Tiger), was ordered to die.
Wang Ling plotted to enthrone Cao Biao and was executed.
Linghu Yu plotted to enthrone Cao Biao.
At Sun Liang's accession rhymes foretold Zhuge Ke's end.
Zhuge Ke was killed and his body thrown into Stone Child Pit, as the rhyme foretold.
Zhuge Rong, younger brother of Zhuge Ke, guarding Gong'an, killed himself by swallowing gold from his seal.
In Sun Xiu's Yong'an 2 a strange child prophesied Sima rule.
Sun Hao took a prophecy as his own, grew more tyrannical, and surrendered.
Wang Jun, nicknamed Atong, was made Dragon-Prancing General and first took Moling.
Emperor Wu of Jin promoted Wang Jun and conquered Wu.
The empress dowager was deposed and died imprisoned.
A strange child appeared among hostage boys and prophesied, claiming to be the planet Mars.
In Emperor Hui's Yongxi era a madman of Wen county wrote prophetic verses.
Yang Jun guarded himself with halberds, monopolized power, and was killed by halberds.
Empress Yang (Yang Zhi), styled Lan, was deposed, starved for eight days by Empress Jia, and buried north of the courier station.
Empress Jia (Nanfeng) starved Empress Yang and plotted against the crown prince.
The Prince of Chu (Sima Wei) held power with Yang Jun.
The crown prince, whose childhood name was Shamen, was endangered by Empress Jia.
Jia Mi, whose fief was Lu, joined Empress Jia's plot.
Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne, was blind in one eye, and was killed by the allied princes.
Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, joined the allied princes, then stayed to assist government with disloyal intent.
Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, joined the allied princes from Ye.
Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, joined the allied princes from Guanzhong.
Emperor Yuan (Sima Rui) succeeded in Jiangdong and ruled only the south.
Sima Yue, styled Yuanchao, returned to Luoyang and grew to hate Gou Xi.
Gou Xi crushed Ji Sang and was stripped of Yan Province by Sima Yue.
Ji Sang was crushed by Gou Xi.
Emperor Min (Sima Ye) surrendered to Liu Yao in Jianxing 4.
Liu Yao received Emperor Min's surrender.
Wang Dun's Shitou incident let troops loot the capital.
Qian Feng attacked the capital again and was driven back.
Shen Chong retreated to Wuxing and was beheaded with his son.
Emperor Ming's Taining rhyme foretold his death.
Emperor Cheng, young, was forced by Su Jun to Stone City and died soon after a rhyme.
Su Jun forced Emperor Cheng to Stone City and soon died.
Su Shi, younger brother of Su Jun, held Shitou and was crushed.
Shi Hu (called Shi Wu in the rhyme) met the fate the Hebei rhyme foretold.
Yu Liang garrisoned Wuchang and died at his post, returning in mourning as the song foretold.
Emperor Mu, called Azi, died in Shengping 5.
The empress dowager wept for Emperor Mu.
Hu Qian interpreted the Integrity Song as foretelling a death.
Emperor Ai changed the era to Xingning to avert a rhyme and died young.
Lord Huan (Huan Wen) was foretold to enter Stone City.
The Duke of Haixi was deposed and his three putative sons strangled.
A man of Wen county, as if mad, wrote prophetic verses.
Shen Chong and his son were beheaded.
The three sons, said not to be the Duke of Haixi's, were strangled with horse reins.
The Duke of Haixi, impotent, had attendants beget sons he passed off as his own.
Huan Shimin governed Jingzhou from Shangming and died.
Wang Chen, styled Huang Tanzi with childhood name Fo Da, succeeded Huan Shimin in Jingzhou as the song foretold.
In late Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Jingkou sang of a yellow hen.
Wang Gong raised troops at Jingkou to kill Wang Guobao, was defeated by Liu Laozhi, and soon died.
Wang Guobao was the target of Wang Gong's troops.
Liu Laozhi defeated Wang Gong.
Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, built Lingxiu Hill; his fief Kuaiji was ravaged by Sun En.
Sun En, styled Lingxiu, rebelled and twice ravaged Kuaiji.
Yu Kai held Liyang, fled south to Huan Xuan, and was executed by him.
Huan Xuan executed Yu Kai, took Jingzhou, usurped, and was killed after fleeing to Jiangling.
Yin Zhongkan in Jingzhou was defeated as a rhyme foretold.
In Emperor An's Long'an and Yixi eras songs foretold Huan Xuan's and Lu Long's falls.
Liu Yu's loyalist forces retook the capital and executed Huan Xuan.
Lu Long was favored by the court, rebelled from Guangzhou, pressed the capital, and failed to take Stone City.
Fu Jian reigned thirty years, was routed at the Fei, and was killed by Yao Chang at Xincheng.
Yao Chang killed Fu Jian.
Murong Chong attacked Fu Jian.
In Emperor Wu's Taikang 6 Nanyang presented a two-legged beast.
The crown prince (Minhuai) was killed in Yuankang 9.
A son was born to the Duke of Haixi's household and celebrated in song.
Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, presented a four-horned beast in Taikang 7 and later raised war from all sides.
In Emperor Huai's Yongjia 5 omens appeared at Yanling and Jiaxing.
Guo Pu divined that a man east of the commandery would claim imperial style and soon die.
Xu Fu of Wuxing rebelled, killed the governor Yuan Xiu, and was soon destroyed.
Grand Administrator Yuan Xiu was killed by Xu Fu.
In Emperor Cheng's Xianhe 6 a deer appeared before the gathered candidates.
Sun Sheng read the deer as auspicious.
In Emperor Ai's Longhe 1 a deer entered the Donghai residence.
The Duke of Haixi was deposed as Prince of Donghai and moved into that residence.
In Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan 13 a rabbit ran across the temple hall.
Zhuge Ke ignored a dog tugging his robe and was killed at court.
Emperor Wu ignored He Qiao and kept Emperor Hui as heir.
He Qiao's advice on the heir was ignored.
Emperor Hui was weak while princes slandered one another.
Danyang Interior Minister Zhu Kui's dog bore headless pups; he was killed by Cao Wu.
Yangzhou inspector Cao Wu killed Zhu Kui.
A dog in Zhang Lin's household at Jiaxing spoke.
In Emperor Min's Jianxing 1 dogs and pigs mated; he died among the barbarians.
In Emperor Yuan's Taixing era omens appeared to Zhang Mao and He Xu.
Wu commandery governor Zhang Mao heard a dog under his bed and was killed by Shen Chong.
Shen Chong killed Zhang Mao.
He Xu of Qian county dug up a dog; his village was later overrun by barbarians.
In Emperor An's early Long'an era dogs howled in Wu commandery.
Sun En rebelled in Wu and Kuaiji.
General Sun Wuzhong found white pups underground and was later exterminated by Huan Xuan.
Huan Xuan exterminated Sun Wuzhong, was soiled by a dog at his investiture as King of Chu, and fell eighty days later.
In Emperor Ming of Wei's Qinglong 3 a meteorite fell at Shouguang.
Sima Yi later took power.
In Sun Liang's Wufeng 2 a great stone stood up at Yangxian.
Sun Hao gained the throne from a deposed house.
Sun Xiu's enthronement was another reading of the standing stone.
In Emperor Wu's Taikang 10 a stone grew at Luoyang; he died the next year.
In Emperor Hui's Yuankang and Yongning eras stone and child omens appeared.
Shi Bing entered Jianye.
Sima Teng, Prince of Dongying and Cavalry Grand General, found a toothless jade horse and was killed by Ji Sang.
Ji Sang killed Sima Teng.
Yi Province inspector Huangfu Yan attacked the Wenshan Hu and was falsely accused and killed by Zhang Hong.
Assistant He Lü remonstrated with Huangfu Yan in vain.
Yamen officer Zhang Hong falsely accused Huangfu Yan and killed him.
Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, raised a righteous army in Yongning 1.
In Emperor Cheng's early Xiankang era fur grew from the earth.
Sun Sheng read ground hair as a sign of human toil.
After Shi Jilong's fall the Central Plain turned to Jin.
In Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era hair grew from the ground; Xie An left for Guangling in his Taiyuan 10.
After Fu Jian's destruction there was much campaigning.
In Emperor An's Long'an 4 the ground grew hair.
Sima Xiuzhi was attacked in the west by the royal army.
At the end of the Prince of Qi's Zhengshi era timber struck a clerk in Li Sheng's hall.
Henan Intendant Li Sheng fell ten days after a timber omen.
Tally clerk Shi Biao was decapitated by falling timber.
Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed and died the year after the altar stone split.
Xie An went to Guangling in Taiyuan 10, fell ill, returned, and died.
An eight-year-old white-haired child from Fanchang divined in Sima Jiong's army.
In Sun Liang's Jianxing 1 and Wufeng 1 out-of-season omens appeared; he was later deposed.
Zhuge Ke began as regent and relaxed Wu's government.
The young emperor of Wei (Cao Huan) ruled indulgently in Jingyuan 3.
Emperor Hui, newly enthroned, failed to see through Sima Wei's forged edict.
Sima Wei, Prince of Chu, forged an edict to kill Sima Liang and Wei Guan.
Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, was killed by Sima Wei's forged edict.
Grand Guardian Wei Guan was killed by Sima Wei's forged edict.
In Emperor Mu's Yonghe 9 peach and plum bloomed while Jianwen governed.
Sima Yu (later Emperor Jianwen) assisted government laxly.
Cao Cao (Wei Wudi) cut bleeding trees for Jianshi Hall, fell ill, and died that month.
That year was Cao Pi's Huangchu 1.
In Liu Shan's Jingyao 5 a palace tree broke; Shu then fell.
Qiao Zhou wrote a riddle on a pillar foretelling Shu's fall.
In Sun Hao's Tianxi 1 Linping Lake reopened; Wu soon fell.
Craftsman Huang Gou, at whose house ghost-eye vegetables grew, was made Attendant of the Fungus.
Craftsman Wu Ping, at whose house a lettuce-like plant grew, was made Gentleman of Pinglü.
Wang Jun's ships stopped at Pingzhu when Wu was conquered.
The crown prince (Minhuai) ignored the mulberry omen and was deposed and killed.
Sun Xiu took charge of affairs, bringing great disorder.
Zhang Lin took charge of affairs, bringing great disorder.
Sima Zang, imperial grandson, was made heir-grandson in Yongkang 1 and poisoned by Sima Lun.
Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped and poisoned Sima Zang.
Zhang Hua, enfeoffed at Zhuangwu, was killed.
In Emperor Huai's Yongjia 2 a mulberry wept at Xiang county; he was later lost to the north.
Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, left the capital, died in Yongjia 5, and his coffin was split and corpse burned by Shi Le.
Shi Le surrounded Sima Yue's army, killed over a hundred thousand, and burned Yue's corpse.
Guo Pu foretold an uncanny tree and a rebellion.
Source-dated attestation retained from Chinese “永嘉六年以後”; Western bound retracted.
Emperor Min was lost to the north.
Emperor Yuan restored Jin in the south.
In Emperor Ming's Taining 1 a tree bore a human face.
Wang Dun rebelled and failed.
In Emperor Cheng's reign dead trees revived at Qu'a and Wu county.
A dead elm revived at Wu Xiong's house in Wu county.
Emperor Kang had been Prince of Wu and kept Wu as his fief before succeeding.
In Emperor Ai's Xingning 3 a dead chestnut revived; he soon died.
A dead chestnut revived at Xiu Ming's house in Xichang county.
Emperor Xiaowu, taboo name Changming, was four years old in Xingning 3 and later succeeded; Lady Zhang monopolized his favor.
The Duke of Haixi succeeded and was soon deposed.
Emperor Jianwen succeeded from a princely fief and reigned under two years.
Zhang Tianxi held power in Liangzhou and surrendered to Fu Jian.
Fu Jian received Zhang Tianxi's surrender.
Lady Zhang monopolized Emperor Xiaowu's favor and was blamed after his death.
In Emperor An's Yuanxing 3 bamboo fruited.
A soldier of the Yangwu General's camp, Chen Gai, had a giant bitter lettuce grow at his house.
Yao Hong was destroyed, ending the campaigns.
Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi) issued an edict after pelicans gathered and died in Huangchu 7.
Yang Biao was recommended.
Guan Ning was recommended.
A swallow hatched a hawk-like chick at Li Gai's house in Weiguo.
Gaotang Long warned of hawk-like ministers and explained the magpie nest to the emperor.
Sima Yi executed Cao Shuang and took control of Wei.
Cao Shuang was executed by Sima Yi.
Cao Cao, King Wu of Wei, died the next year.
Emperor Ming of Wei (Cao Rui) dreaded the pelicans, asked Gaotang Long about magpies, and died at the end of Jingchu.
In Liu Shan's Jianxing 9 birds drowned crossing the Yangtze.
Zhuge Liang campaigned yearly against the north and died south of the Wei River.
Sun Quan had Zhu Ju burn a magpie; his heirs and ministers then suffered.
Acting Chancellor Zhu Ju burned the magpie and was later demoted.
Crown Prince Sun He was deposed.
Sun Ba, Prince of Lu, was ordered to die.
Lu Yi (Lu Xun) died of grief.
In Sun Quan's Taiyuan 2 the former heir He was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.
Sun He, former crown prince, was made Prince of Nanyang, sent to Changsha, and later died a violent death.
In Sun Liang's Jianxing 2 five great birds appeared and the era was changed to Wufeng; he lacked virtuous government.
Sun Jun was arrogant and violent.
Sun Hao changed the era after a supposed phoenix in Jianheng 3.
In Emperor Wu's Taishi 4 a pheasant perched on Changhe Gate; he died four years after Taikang 7.
In Emperor Hui's Yongkang 1 and Yuankang 5 omens appeared.
Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped, imprisoned a strange bird and a boy, had an eye tumor, and was executed.
In Emperor Huai's Yongjia 1 geese emerged from a sinkhole at Luoyang.
Dong Yang of Chenliu interpreted the geese as barbarian invasion.
Liu Yuanhai ravaged China.
Shi Le ravaged China.
Two great birds appeared under Emperor Ming, who died in the intercalary month.
Su Jun rebelled, burned the palace, and confined the emperor and Wang Dao at Shitou.
Zu Yue rebelled with Su Jun.
In Emperor Cheng's Xianhe 2 gulls gathered; he was confined at Shitou with Wang Dao.
Yu Liang ignored counsel and summoned Su Jun.
Emperor Kang had just acceded in Xiankang 8 and died within two years.
The Duke of Haixi acceded in Xingning 3 and was deposed by Huan Wen.
Huan Wen deposed the Duke of Haixi.
In Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan 16 magpies nested on palace and academy roofs; after his death Huan Xuan usurped.
Emperor An succeeded Xiaowu.
Huan Xuan usurped the throne.
Dragon-Prancing General Zhu Yi garrisoned Shouyang and died the next year after a crow omen.
Minister over the Masses Wang Dao's sheep was born without hind legs; he was confined at Shitou with the emperor.
Feng Yun ravaged Xuzhou killing tens of thousands.
A boy named the strange bird and was locked up by Sima Lun, then vanished.
A maid cooking rice at Zhu Yi's camp failed to drive away crows.
Crown Prince Minhuai was sent to confinement at Xu palace and was killed that month in Yongkang 1.
Emperor Hui was dull and did not awaken to the omen.
In Emperor Min's Jianxing 1 Hedong quaked and meat rained.
Transport supervisor clerk Chunyu Bo was executed under military law; his blood flowed up a pillar.
Rear General Chu Pou guarded Guangling.
The Chancellor (Sima Rui, later Emperor Yuan) proclaimed a northern campaign and, as emperor, did not punish the officials.
Gan Bao read the drought as response to an unjust death.
Guo Pu read the upward-flowing blood as a sign of governmental error.
Liu Cong, in his illegitimate Jianyuan 1, saw meat fall at Pingyang and took three daughters of Liu Yin as empresses.
Liu Yin's three daughters became Liu Cong's empresses.
Liu Cong's empress née Liu bore a snake and a beast; the three Liu empresses later died.
Chunyu Bo's son appealed that his father's crimes did not merit death.
